title: Shortcut Conflict shown when there's no documented conflict.
author: gungfujoe
summary: PowerToys 0.101.2362 reports Win+Shift+C as a system shortcut conflict even though Color Picker still receives the shortcut and the linked Windows shortcut documentation does not list that chord.

status.label: Design investigation ready
status.detail: The current reproduction and conflict-detector implementation are specific enough for code investigation.

next_action.label: Investigate conflict attribution
next_action.reason: Distinguish reserved system hotkeys from other registration failures and avoid unsupported ownership claims.

judgment.rationale: This appears to be a current 0.101 behavior, but the evidence supports a conflict-attribution/design investigation rather than a confirmed root cause.
evidence: The reporter reproduced on 0.101.2362 after manually updating.
Win+Shift+C still opens Color Picker, so there is no functional activation failure.
The UI labels the conflict as a system shortcut and links to Windows documentation that the reporter says has no Win+Shift+C entry.
hotkey_conflict_detector.cpp treats RegisterHotKey ERROR_HOTKEY_ALREADY_REGISTERED as a system conflict even though that failure can also mean another application owns the chord.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a focused design for conflict attribution and wording; do not expose approve_design until an implementation-grade fix plan exists.

issue_context.summary: The conflict detector labels a functioning Color Picker chord as a Windows system conflict and points users to documentation that does not support the classification.
known_information: The configured chord is Win+Shift+C for Color Picker.
The home screen displays one shortcut conflict.
The shortcut still opens Color Picker.
The reporter confirmed the same behavior after updating to PowerToys 0.101.2362.
No assignee, duplicate, or linked fix is present.
inferences: The conflict probe may be detecting a registration failure without enough evidence to identify Windows as the owner.
Color Picker may use a different activation path from the conflict probe, allowing the shortcut to work despite the warning.
issue_context.analysis: The current report is specific and already validated on 0.101.2362. More reporter data is unlikely to change the next step; maintainers need to inspect the detector semantics and UI attribution.
initial_investigation: src/runner/hotkey_conflict_detector.cpp::HasConflictWithSystemHotkey uses RegisterHotKey with a temporary id.
The same code returns true on ERROR_HOTKEY_ALREADY_REGISTERED and GetAllConflicts surfaces that as System ownership.
Targeted issue search found this issue as the only open Win+Shift+C conflict report.
